title: experiment(wren): evaluate RP2040 runtime memory and SRAM-only feasibility
body:
Evaluate official Wren for KAGURA Desktop, isolated under `experiments/wren-rp2040/`. MicroPython remains the baseline. **Keep this PR Draft; no automatic merge.**

Includes the pinned official VM (99d2f0b8fc2686134b32b18166e037639f7e9f2c, MIT), a minimal bidirectional C host, ten original deterministic workloads, UTF-8 checks, embedded GC configuration, allocation instrumentation, OOM containment, PC measurements and reproducible RP2040 no_flash builds. No C Desktop, MicroPython SDK, RTL, ABI, firmware, GUI, IME or filesystem integration changes.

### Memory audit findings

See `MEMORY_ANALYSIS.md` for the complete phase-by-phase audit and conservative budgets.

- **98,239 B is maximum concurrently live Wren-requested payload**, produced by string creation/concatenation. It is not a single allocation or allocator footprint. Largest single request: 8,192 B. That workload has 480,242 B cumulative request traffic and a 132,432 B newlib arena high-water in fresh-process ARM emulation.
- A separate persistent GUI model tests a Japanese title, rectangle, four events, compiled callbacks and real C foreign calls. With repeated script/GC/error checks over 20 lifecycles, its minimums are 90,437 B requested and 124,240 B bounded allocator capacity. A practical emulated 96 KiB payload / 128 KiB arena passes 100 lifecycles, including recovery after actual malloc failure in the same unchanged arena.
- The proposed smallest positive hardware profile is that GUI model over 20 VMs, with 96 KiB payload cap, 132 KiB physical arena and 48 KiB native stack, retaining the existing error/OOM checks and requiring observed recovery margins.
- **The old 32 KiB native stack was inadequate.** ARM stack painting observes 33,840 B for the GUI/simple workloads and 39,940 B for fibers. Current builds enforce at least 48 KiB and reject the retired image.
- Independently verified guarded SRAM layouts leave 77,392 B malloc by default, or 85,584 B when the core-0 stack extends through the unused scratch banks. Linker assertions and symbol checks prevent scratch/core-1 overlap. Wren-only LTO enlarged the image. Neither configuration can run positive GUI acceptance; even the old hypothetical 104,256 B region is below initializer footprint.
- A conservative flash-resident Wren + existing retained C Desktop budget is 281 KiB: RP2040 is 17 KiB short; RP2350 has 239 KiB spare. These are planning estimates, not an integrated firmware measurement. Standalone SRAM code size is not treated as integrated RAM use.

### Validation and limits

Original correctness/OOM tests are retained, with added GUI, allocator and layout checks. Release and ASan/UBSan pass. ARM phase sweeps, bounded-arena bisections, 100-cycle failure recovery, three Pico cross-builds, ELF/UF2 validation and malformed-image rejection checks pass. The positive-profile arena gate correctly rejects every current SRAM candidate.

All runtime measurements are PC-hosted or CPU emulation, clearly labelled. Existing Stage 3A host/static results remain provisional reference inputs. Wren 0.4.0 was rejected for a reproduced aggressive-GC ASan defect; the selected official revision contains its upstream fix.

**No physical hardware was accessed or executed, and no hardware approval is requested.** A positive SRAM-only RP2040 VM/GUI test is not practical with the current image, allocator and safe stack reservation. OOM/boot recovery alone would not establish runtime acceptance. Firmware restoration and full-flash hash verification remain unperformed future acceptance gates.

title: experiment: minimal flash-resident Wren Desktop on RP2040
body:
This isolated experiment combines pinned C Desktop (#68) and Wren (#69) sources without changing either implementation or software/. One native desktop retains its 32,000-byte framebuffer. The four-method Wren API uses synchronous acknowledged TILE4 export and guarded snapshot/export storage sharing.

**Physical RP2040 runtime, memory, full-plane CRC and OOM validation completed on 2026-11-03. Original MicroPython flash was restored and verified by full 2 MiB ROM readback and a device-side rehash.** This is a minimal feasibility result, not long-duration qualification. The retained HDMI colour-comparison caveat is below.

Tested firmware source: 0aa0974938a150d84bccf98dae7482977f17926c.
ELF SHA-256: c35cd4a58c75907215b183616516eb16bd0cd89e74080aa59a0be4977123bd2b.
Hardware: Pico RP2040 B2, 125 MHz, Tang Nano 9K ABI 0.6 / CAPS 0x5b, QSPI 5 MHz / four lanes.

Actual results:
- Static SRAM 45,556 B; bounded native arena 135,168 B; unchanged 49,152 B stack and 8,192 B recovery reserve; 32,268 B (31.51 KiB) unassigned. Linked reservation is 3,216 B below the prior estimate.
- Peak Wren payload 91,970 B; native arena peak 126,476 B; painted stack upper bound 33,760 B; bottom/recovery canaries intact.
- All seven 32,000-byte FPGA plane readbacks match the native framebuffer byte-for-byte and the host CRC goldens.
- Twenty compiled application callbacks, three expected OOM paths and twenty subsequent fresh VMs pass with zero live VM ledger blocks after cleanup.
- Compiled App.run() averages 49.505 ms for five presents/four events; explicit GC averages 1.370 ms. Foreign body times and measurement boundaries are in HARDWARE.md.
- Host Release 18/18, ASan/UBSan 18/18, unchanged Wren baseline 1/1, ARM-emulated correctness/CRC/allocation-cap/malloc recovery pass.

The first physical run exposed Pico SDK's default malloc-panic policy. Its failure evidence is retained and original flash was restored/verified before correction. The corrected SDK policy returns NULL to the existing whole-VM discard path; hard sbrk bounds, explicit allocation range checks, stack MPU guard and watchdog remain enabled. No correctness/OOM test or reservation was weakened.

HDMI visibly shows the title/rectangle/event sequence. The unchanged capture colour classifier retains 46 unexplained pixels on the thin red outline. A supplementary fixed geometry check finds all 140 expected red pixels with no extras/missing, and the FPGA readback is exact, but this does not waive the original colour-test discrepancy. Absolute HDMI colour fidelity remains open.

Programming/restoration was restricted to 0x10000000–0x10026000; complete readbacks verify the unchanged tail.
Original and restored full-flash SHA-256: d2ccc104c2a14a84e56501632ceb2ef802f3ad39c3493f42eba83c547f14987b.
Healthy MicroPython v1.26.0 startup and KAGURA console communication are confirmed.

See experiments/wren-desktop/HARDWARE.md for exact revisions, raw logs, screenshots, latency/memory metrics, the initial failure, emulation differences and restoration verification. Flash/filesystem backups remain local and are not published. The loaded FPGA bitstream hash is not independently established; ABI/CAPS are verified.

No FPGA firmware change, foreign API expansion, Japanese font integration or merge occurred. Keep PRs #68, #69 and #70 Draft and unmerged.

title: experiment: reusable Native C Japanese Text Engine
body:
Native Desktop window titles currently count UTF-8 bytes as ASCII glyphs, so Japanese becomes replacement characters and can be truncated in the middle of a character. This adds a reusable C11 text engine and an optional native-title adapter: “神楽 Desktop” now renders and measures as mixed text while existing ASCII/GUI images remain byte-identical.

The independent library provides strict UTF-8 decoding with documented one-invalid-byte recovery, validated KJ8F lookup/fallback, measurement, clipped pixel targets and bounded packed 4bpp drawing. It reuses the complete existing 7,171-glyph Misaki asset verbatim, preserves its separate license/attribution, allocates no heap or glyph cache, and needs no Wren, MicroPython, OS or FPGA API. Native integration is guarded by KD_NATIVE_TEXT; title storage stays 24 bytes and copies complete decoded units.

Measured Cortex-M0+ / GCC 14.2.1 / -Os budget:
- Full portable core object: 2,055 B read-only; font+descriptor: 71,742 B; native adapter: 347 B; each has zero writable static RAM.
- Identical minimal Desktop link: 12,088 → 85,792 B ROM, **+73,704 B ROM / +0 B static RAM**.
- Desktop remains 34,160 B, including the original 32,000-byte framebuffer. The host demo streams image output without a second framebuffer.
- Largest compiler engine frame: 200 B; direct packed-draw chain estimate ~424 B before caller/callback/interrupts. This is static analysis, not a physical stack measurement. PR #70’s 48 KiB reservation is unchanged.

Validation: standalone core 2/2, Release integration/native regression 21/21, ASan/UBSan 21/21, original opt-out Desktop baseline 17/17. All 1,112,064 Unicode scalar roundtrips, 85,547 CPython strict-decoder cases, all 7,171 source glyphs, clipping/bounds/dirty-tile/title-copy/overlap/painter checks pass. All 26 existing ASCII/GUI reference images match the opt-out build byte-for-byte. Native Japanese title/overlap/reveal screenshots and complete maps/logs are in experiments/native-text/results/.

This Draft is stacked on Draft #70 solely to keep the review diff focused; the text library has no runtime dependency on it. PRs #68 and #70 stay Draft, unmodified and unmerged. MicroPython/Wren/ABI/firmware sources are unchanged. No hardware was accessed or flashed. No SKK, IME, editor or Wren bindings are added.

experiments/native-text/README.md documents the API, exact license/source hashes, reproduction and the next separate Wren step: checked length-bounded title transfer into native ownership, no VM font copy, then FFI/GC/OOM/CRC tests and a fresh integrated linker map.

title: Stage 4: Wren Native Japanese Desktop integration
body:
Stage 4 connects PR #71’s unchanged Native C Japanese Text Engine and complete Misaki font with PR #70’s protected Wren Desktop. Wren creates “神楽 Desktop” from a temporary UTF-8 string, releases it and runs GC before native rendering.

**Separately approved physical validation completed on 2026-11-03. Japanese HDMI, all seven full-plane FPGA CRCs, repeated GC/VM lifecycle, expected OOM recovery and memory guards pass. Original MicroPython was restored and verified by complete 2 MiB readback and device rehash.** The historical 46-pixel thin-red colour-classification caveat remains open.

The existing four-method API is retained. open(_) uses explicit Wren byte length, validates the complete span up to 1024 bytes, rejects malformed UTF-8/NUL/C0/DEL, and copies at most 23 whole-codepoint bytes into the unchanged 24-byte native title. No VM pointer/font copy, second framebuffer or GUI structure growth is introduced. Private compiled-call tickets reject stale/released handles before Wren C API use.

Validation:
- Stage 4 Release and ASan/UBSan: 5/5 each.
- Original PR #70: 18/18 Release and 18/18 sanitizer tests.
- Original PR #71: 21/21 Release and 21/21 sanitizer tests.
- Original Wren feasibility: 1/1.
- ARM fixed-arena correctness, cap sweeps, twenty-VM/compiled-call runs and native/requested OOM recovery pass.
- Seven normal and ten overlap/reveal/move native/Wren/ARM frames agree. ASCII matches #70’s original goldens exactly. Physical acceptance is the minimal one-window image; extended overlap/movement capture is not claimed.

Actual complete RP2040 link vs physically validated #70:
- Flash load payload 227,480 B (+74,648).
- Static SRAM 45,596 B (+40 for private call/session state).
- Allocator 135,168 B / stack 49,152 B / recovery 8,192 B unchanged.
- Unassigned SRAM 32,228 B (-40), with physical-bank accounting.
- All 71,718 font bytes remain in flash. DesktopState stays 34,284 B including the sole 32,000-byte framebuffer.

Real RP2040:
- Peak requested payload 91,994 B; ledger peak 111,418 B; arena 126,436 B; used occupancy 122,796 B.
- Stack painted upper bound 33,848 B; bottom/recovery canaries intact.
- Twenty compiled callbacks and twenty fresh VMs after three OOM paths pass, with zero live VM blocks after cleanup.
- App.run averages 53.711 ms for five presents/four events; explicit GC 1.381 ms. These include additional script GC/string work and are not isolated font-cost measurements.

The first 0.33-second captures were black/no-signal despite correct runtime/CRC checks; evidence is retained and MicroPython was restored/verified. The exact same ELF succeeded with 3-second receiver settling and a no-signal abort check. No target firmware, FPGA bitstream, colour tolerance or protection was changed. The unchanged full classifier reproduces only the historical 46 unexplained red-outline pixels, with no additional unexplained Japanese-title pixels.

Tested firmware source: 25c7e9c03a5bfe6508dea91ee3faeebb0a57874d.
ELF SHA-256: af6f1679e7b1e4577bec5eca6d0781aacb3ffa527aa07215cddb04a2bbf456f9.
Approved/programmed/restored prefix: 0x10000000–0x10038000 only.
Programmed full-flash SHA-256: 98526fd2dfd1e975cce83e4c6f232c6a64aa194fa05f4b0c91b87674b4d864ab.
Original/restored complete-flash SHA-256: d2ccc104c2a14a84e56501632ceb2ef802f3ad39c3493f42eba83c547f14987b.
Healthy MicroPython v1.26.0 and KAGURA console/HDMI are confirmed. Private backups are not published.

See experiments/wren-japanese-desktop/README.md and HARDWARE.md for policies, maps/program headers, bank-level memory, measured/emulated comparisons, screenshots, raw logs, capture diagnostics and restoration proofs. This Draft is stacked on #71 for focused review. References #68/#69/#70/#71 remain unchanged Drafts; original evidence and tests are preserved. No IME/editor/filesystem work, renderer redesign, FPGA change, guard reduction or merge occurred.

title: Desktop: establish native and Wren module boundaries (Stage 5)
body:
The validated Japanese Desktop currently builds through a flat Wren integration archive and nested experimental CMake projects. This adds explicit native text, GUI, application/transport and Wren build boundaries under `software/desktop`, while retaining the verified C implementation and historical entry points. Native C applications now configure, link and run without Wren or MicroPython. Generated application source goes into the build tree; the original generator default remains compatible.

This is the first, deliberately limited consolidation step. It still references experimental source paths; physical source moves are specified as small follow-up PRs. No renderer rewrite, foreign API expansion, Japanese menus/dialogs, IME, scheduler or editor is included.

Based on the exact PR #72 head `e2ff7ead9144136e95096a92e0d024ee051b3f66`. Keep this PR and #68–#72 Draft and unmerged.

### Audit and design

- [Architecture/dependency diagrams, public boundaries and ownership](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-foundation/software/desktop/docs/architecture.md): actual ancestry includes #68/#69 via #70, then #71/#72; one Desktop/framebuffer, synchronous acknowledged TILE4 and shared scratch lifetime are preserved.
- [Japanese GUI and application specification](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-foundation/software/desktop/docs/japanese-gui.md): native text measurement/clipping, menu/dialog/focus contracts, bounded 2,288-byte pool proposal, explicit session/handle lifecycle. Design only.
- [Staged PR sequence, dependencies, rollback and risks](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-foundation/software/desktop/docs/plan.md): no wholesale merge of the experiments; source ownership and shared platform policy move separately.
- [Complete validation/memory report](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-foundation/software/desktop/docs/validation.md), [linker map](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-foundation/software/desktop/results/flash-linker.map), and [ELF/load comparison](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-foundation/software/desktop/results/load-equivalence.json).

### Validation

111 CTest invocations passed: consolidated Release + ASan/UBSan (8 each), all retained #70/#71/#72/#69 Release + sanitizer suites (18/21/5/1 each), and runtime-free native configuration (5). Existing mutation tests, ASCII goldens, malformed UTF-8, window overlap/reveal/move, allocation limits, GC and OOM recovery assertions remain unchanged. SDL interactive smoke was not selected.

All seven normal and ten overlap/move CRCs match the fresh reference. Fourteen Wren/native streaming image files and three native title-demo files are byte-identical to their references. The native-only application matches the seven Wren CRCs; native archives have no VM or malloc dependency. Source provenance verifies 41 implementation inputs unchanged from the base.

Cortex-M0+ CPU/newlib emulation passed unchanged correctness/OOM acceptance, 20-cycle lifecycle/recovery cases and budget/capacity sweeps. Peak payload 91,994 B, payload+ledger 111,418 B, backing 128,640 B, painted stack 33,648 B. The 8-byte backing difference from historical #72 emulation is arena-base alignment: both reach `0x64000`; it is not an optimization or a new safe hardware minimum.

### Linked RP2040 budget

| Resource | Actual | Delta from #72 / prior estimate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Flash payload | 227,480 B | 0 |
| Static SRAM | 45,596 B | 0 |
| Bounded Wren arena | 135,168 B | 0 |
| Native stack reservation | 49,152 B | 0 |
| Recovery reservation | 8,192 B | 0 |
| Unassigned SRAM | 32,228 B | 0 |

Unassigned means 24,036 B in the main address range plus separate 4,096 B X/Y banks, not one contiguous heap. The 32,000-byte framebuffer is already included in the 34,284-byte owner. Stack guards, OOM handling, watchdog, recovery and arena boundaries are preserved.

Every PT_LOAD address, reservation size, flags/alignment and initialized byte matches a freshly rebuilt #72 entry point in the same checkout. Whole ELF SHA differs due to nonloaded build/debug information; both hashes and per-segment hashes are retained. Consolidated ELF SHA-256: `3a756660250a006e4df3a1317835cd2ec8eec29c1a4328e559c2086d5e64f6be`.

No hardware access, Flash programming or physical execution occurred. Historical #72 hardware figures (126,436 B backing / 33,848 B stack) remain historical; simulation/static identity is not new physical acceptance. The existing HDMI 46-pixel red-outline classification discrepancy remains unresolved, with thresholds unchanged. The original MicroPython and native implementations, font/license, FPGA ABI and unrelated working-tree changes are untouched.

title: Desktop: move native core and graphics into canonical source ownership
body:
The new Desktop targets still compiled native GUI code from experimental source paths. This moves the existing native application/window/compositor sources to `software/desktop/core` and raster/regions/TILE4/ASCII sources to `software/desktop/gfx`, establishing one canonical source owner without changing implementation bytes.

Stacked on Draft PR #73, exact base `0214429bd0cde433fab111e7acb78bc1b3f22a3a`. This is only consolidation-plan step 2; text/runtime/platform relocation remains separate. Keep this PR and #68–#73 Draft and unmerged.

### Scope and compatibility

- All 18 files (nine C, nine headers) preserve their original Git blobs and license notices. Public include names and C behavior are unchanged.
- New targets compile canonical sources directly. Old source/header paths are forwarding files for existing CMake, explicit ARM scripts and binding source lists. Compile either route, never both.
- The ASCII generator now checks/writes the canonical font table; the host preview reads the canonical palette source. No glyph, generator output, palette, regression assertion or golden changed.
- Native text, application owner, Wren, HAL, MicroPython implementation, FPGA ABI, allocator/OOM handling, guards and watchdog are unchanged. A complete MicroPython firmware rebuild is not claimed.

[Source ownership, compatibility, measurements and rollback report](https://github.com/siska-tech/kagura/blob/refactor/desktop-native-ownership/software/desktop/docs/native-ownership.md)

### Validation

114 CTest invocations passed: canonical Release + ASan/UBSan 9 each; retained legacy #70/#71/#72/#69 suites 18/21/5/1 each in both modes; runtime-free build 6. All thirteen GUI mutation variants remain. The initial legacy font check caught the old generator output path; the path was adapted without changing the check or generated bytes. SDL interactive smoke was not selected.

Seven normal and ten overlap/move CRCs, fourteen streaming image hashes and three native title-demo files match. Comparisons require both current compatibility-route output and the frozen PR #73 checked-in baseline, rather than comparing only two routes to the relocated implementation. Native-only code remains free of Wren/MicroPython/malloc dependencies. Source provenance verifies 41 implementation inputs, including every relocated file, against PR #73.

Cortex-M0+ CPU/newlib emulation passed unchanged correctness, repeated lifecycle/GC, budget and arena sweeps, malloc-limit/OOM recovery and minimum searches. The unchanged legacy explicit ARM script also compiles through the forwarders and passes integration correctness. Host preview PNG is byte-identical using the existing Windows Python/Pillow environment; no package installation was needed.

### RP2040 result

| Resource | Linked / measured | Delta from PR #73 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Flash load payload | 227,480 B | 0 |
| Static SRAM | 45,596 B | 0 |
| Wren arena reservation | 135,168 B | 0 |
| Native stack reservation | 49,152 B | 0 |
| Recovery reserve | 8,192 B | 0 |
| Total unassigned SRAM | 32,228 B | 0 |
| Emulated payload / ledger peak | 91,994 / 111,418 B | 0 |
| Emulated actual allocator backing | 128,640 B | 0 |
| Emulated painted stack upper usage | 33,648 B | 0 |

Estimated growth before measurement was zero; actual growth is zero. Unassigned SRAM is 24,036 B in the main address range plus separate 4,096 B X/Y banks, not one heap. One 34,284-byte Desktop owner still includes its sole 32,000-byte framebuffer and shared 1,280-byte scratch. No new GUI hierarchy, display buffer, cache or allocator was added.

Every PT_LOAD address, reservation size, flags/alignment and initialized byte matches both the frozen PR #73 baseline and a freshly built compatibility-route ELF. Complete ELF SHA differs due to nonloaded source-path/debug information. New ELF SHA-256: `3a7a578ecfd9c475c0a052b7560ddb2ceeb9641b8d88f5bc615fc8c84976f055`. Full map, sections, symbols, stack frames, source hashes and raw test logs are retained under `software/desktop/results`.

No hardware access, Flash programming or physical execution occurred. These static/emulated results do not constitute new physical acceptance. The HDMI 46-pixel red-outline classification discrepancy remains unresolved, with thresholds unchanged. No Japanese menus/dialogs, IME, scheduler, editor or new foreign API is included.
